## Context

The shared server in  currently sends a fixed  bytes and then sleeps 0.1 seconds; every delayed wake-up permanently reduces cumulative throughput.

## Plan

1. Quantify the existing fixed-sleep drift with a deterministic pacing test and a controlled contention reproduction.
2. Change only the shared test server's dribble scheduler to derive bytes owed from elapsed monotonic time. After a delayed wake-up it catches up to the configured cumulative byte budget instead of treating the delay as lost sending time.
3. Exercise both consumers of the shared fixture: all stall/dribble cases in  and . Keep zero-byte stall mode unchanged.
4. Verify  has no diff, so the 1000 B/s production floor and 10-second production window remain unchanged.

This changes the fixture's pacing invariant rather than merely raising its rate or widening a finite timing margin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deterministic test proves delayed scheduler wake-ups no longer reduce cumulative dribble throughput.
- [ ] Under controlled contention, all dribble cases in both consumer modules remain non-stall failures.
- [ ] All zero-byte stall cases in both consumer modules still fail specifically as stalls.
- [ ]  is empty; production stall behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

The full suite passed 11,881 tests and failed only the named dribble test with ; an unchanged isolated rerun passed.
